text:
The Flyers arrive at Edmonton on game four of a five-game road trip, fresh off a 3-1 win at Vancouver that snapped a three-game winless run (0-2-1). They're 2-2-1 in their last five and are without Rasmus Ristolainen. The Oilers, on game four of a four-game home stand, beat the Rangers 3-1 behind Devon Levi, who saved 2.6 goals more than the shots deserved. They're missing Isaac Howard.

Our numbers favor Edmonton, 3.14 expected goals to 2.60. Expected goals measure the quality of chances, and at five on five the Oilers have taken 49% of them against 42% for Philadelphia. One caution: Edmonton's results run ahead of its chances. Finishing (20.4 more goals than those chances usually produce) is doing much of the lifting. The Oilers also take 4.2 penalties a game, which keeps handing opponents power plays. In net, projected starter Dan Vladar sits at -0.77 goals saved above expected this season, after +12.74 last year. Levi, also projected, is at +1.49 and has no goalie numbers from last season.

Leon Draisaitl, with goals in four straight, has a 51% chance to score, and Connor McDavid, on a 19-game point streak, has a 94% chance of a point. For Philadelphia, Matvei Michkov's ice time is under scrutiny. As Charlie O'Connor of PHLY Sports posted, "Flyers up 2-0. Konecny on the PP, off a hell of a feed from Michkov." Colton Dach could return for Edmonton and play his 100th NHL game.
